case_name: State of Uttar Pradesh v Jodha Singh and Others
facts: While the II-Temp. Civil and Sessions Judge, Budaun convicted respondents 1 to 7 under sections 147/148 IPC, section 302 read with section 149 IPC (2 counts) and section 307 read with section 149 IPC and sentenced them to imprisonment for life for the conviction under section 302 read with section 149 IPC and to lesser terms of imprisonment for the convictions under the other charges...
The prosecution examined seven witnesses among whom PW 1 Jagdish Singh, PW 2 Ram Din and PW 3 Bangali Singh were eye witnesses.
On the day of occurrence viz. 19-11-1972, the two deceased and PW 1 went to the 'pair' (grain storage yard) to pay off the money due by them to one Soni.
...the accused ran away from the scene.
Jai Ram Singh and Nathu Singh succumbed to the injuries sustained by them at the spot itself.
PW 1 went to the police station at Bilsi and lodged a report Ex. Ka-1 at 6.30 P.M.
A-2 had appeared at the police station at 5.30 P.M. and lodged a report Ex. Ka-8 against four persons viz. Jai Ram Singh, Nathu Singh PW 1 and PW 3.
issues: Whether the accused were present at the scene of occurrence?
Whether the occurrence took place in the manner spoken to by PWs 1 to 3?
Whether the injuries sustained by A-2 and A-3 were caused by PW 1 when he wielded his lathi in defence?
petitioner_arguments: The prosecution case that A-7 had used the tamancha against A-2 in order to create evidence in their favour was too unnatural a version to merit acceptance.

There was no motive for the accused to commit the crime and on the contrary it was the deceased and PW 1 who were aggrieved with A-1 for his having refused to appear as a defence witness on their behalf in the case filed against them under section 307 IPC.
respondent_arguments: The Sessions Judge found the accused guilty of the offence of rioting, murder and attempt to commit murder and sentenced all of them to suffer imprisonment for life for the conviction under section 302 read with section 149 IPC.
The defence set up by the accused was that only A-2 and A-3 were present at the scene and not the other accused.
court_reasoning: After a detailed and careful consideration of the evidence adduced by the prosecution and the defence, the learned Sessions Judge came to the conclusion that all the seven accused persons should have been present at the scene and that the occurrence should have taken place in the manner spoken to by PWs 1 to 3.

The High Court deemed it fit to allow the appeals preferred by the accused despite noticing that 'the learned counsel for the appellants has not disputed that the incident took place near about the time mentioned by the prosecution', and that 'the location at which the incident took place cannot also be doubted.'
holding: The State of U.P. has preferred this appeal against the acquittal of the respondents.
The High Court set aside the convictions awarded to the accused and acquitted them of all the charges framed against them.
cases_cited: State of Uttar Pradesh v Jodha Singh
